title: Does DPO Quietly Induce Emergent Misalignment? Probing Preference-Trained Personas

original_idea.body:
# Does DPO Quietly Induce Emergent Misalignment? Probing Preference-Trained Personas

**Problem:** Success state: we can rule out (or quantify) whether standard preference optimization on a narrow preference dataset spills over into broad misalignment, an open question flagged in the subfield. Most EM work uses SFT; the DPO generalization dynamics are unstudied empirically at accessible scale.

**Direction:** Construct a narrow DPO preference set where 'chosen' responses encode a subtly bad trait (e.g., always confidently wrong, or covertly manipulative) in one domain. DPO-tune a small open model with TRL, then evaluate broad misalignment on unrelated prompts and measure shift along a toxic-persona direction. Compare to SFT on the same content.

**Why it matters:** DPO is the dominant cheap alignment method in the open community. If DPO can leak misalignment like SFT, that reshapes safety guidance for everyone fine-tuning open models — a medium-horizon risk labs underweight.

**Relevant context:** Subfield open problem explicitly asks whether RLHF/DPO can trigger EM via similar generalization. TRL provides DPO. Wang et al. and Persona Vectors give the activation-space toxic-persona direction methodology.
